channel.title: Netability Singapore — Posts
channel.description: Insights and updates on IT security, cloud and MAS compliance from Netability Singapore.

item.title: Nagios 2026R2: what landed across XI, Log Server, Network Analyzer and Fusion
item.description: Nagios has published the on-demand recording of its 2026R2 round-up webinar, held on 29 October. It walks through the September releases across all four commercial products, and it is the fastest way to see what changed without reading four changelogs.

item.title: Your outsourcing register is about to become a third-party register
item.description: On 6 March 2026 MAS issued Consultation Paper P004-2026, proposing Guidelines on Third-Party Risk Management. The consultation closed on 20 April 2026 and the final Guidelines are still pending. When they are issued, the proposed transition period is six months.

item.title: Your AI agents hold credentials — do you know what they can reach?
item.description: For two years the question about AI was what a model might say. That question has moved on. Agents now act — reading mail, querying systems, calling APIs, making changes. They hold credentials. The risk is no longer a bad answer; it is an unauthorised action taken at machine spe…

item.title: FAA-N16: the real gap is retrieval, not recording
item.description: FAA-N16 (Amendment) 2025 took effect on 29 December 2025. Licensed and exempt financial advisers must audio-record pre-transaction call-backs to Selected Clients and to clients of Selected Representatives, and the Notice now prescribes what those call-backs have to cover.

item.title: Nagios Fusion 2026R2: rebuilt interface, live event collection and role-based access
item.description: Nagios has released Fusion 2026R2, and it is the most substantial change to the product in years — a full rebuild on Laravel and React, with a redesigned interface, new dashboards and a role-based permission system.

item.title: MAS AI risk guidelines are coming - The work to start now is your AI inventory
item.description: MAS issued its consultation paper on Guidelines for AI Risk Management in November 2025. The consultation closed on 31 January 2026, and this month MAS Chairman and Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said the Guidelines will be finalised soon.

item.title: New service: continuous MAS Cyber Hygiene scoring and board reporting
item.description: We've launched a dedicated MAS Cyber Hygiene service for financial institutions in Singapore — continuous assessment across all six domains of the Notice, with scored reports ready for management and board review at any time.

item.title: SSL/TLS certificates are getting shorter — here's the timeline to 47 days
item.description: The industry is phasing out long-lived SSL/TLS certificates. Following CA/Browser Forum Ballot SC-081v3 — approved in April 2025 — the maximum validity of a public certificate drops from 398 days today to just 47 days by 2029.

item.title: MAS FAA-N16 voice recording amendments: what financial advisers must do before the deadline
item.description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore amended Notice FAA-N16 on 29 December 2025, tightening requirements for the recording and retention of client communications. Licensed and exempt financial advisers now face clearer obligations around mobile call capture and audit trails.

item.title: Why network microsegmentation stops ransomware where firewalls can't
item.description: Traditional perimeter security assumes threats come from outside. But once an attacker is inside your network, a flat network lets them move laterally to critical systems within minutes.

item.title: Netability marks over 20 years of IT engineering across Singapore, Switzerland and Hong Kong
item.description: Since 2003, we've grown from a Swiss-born system integrator into a trusted partner for Singapore enterprises and MAS-regulated financial institutions. Our approach hasn't changed: honesty, team spirit, and trust — the Neta-Way.
